label: Milk tea
note: Either the leaves are boiled in the milk (masala chai, doodh pati) or strong tea is made first and milk added (Mongolian suutei tsai, which is salted). Hong Kong-style milk tea is finished with evaporated milk.

about.text: A family of drinks that combine tea and milk, hot or cold, often with spices or sweetener. Some are brewed in milk, others have milk added to strong tea.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Two ways: simmer tea leaves (and spices) in milk, or brew tea in water, boil it again and stir milk in; Mongolian and Tibetan grassland tea is salted, Hong Kong tea takes evaporated milk.

processing.text: Or tea is brewed in water, boiled again and the milk stirred in.
